title: Surface Roughness Analysis - Mounds Detection on Teron SL650
subtitle: Post-Oxidation Quality Validation for 10nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Anna Petrova

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron SL650 system to detect and classify Mounds defects during post-oxidation inspection at the 10nm technology node. The test is conducted at Pyeongtaek Fab 2 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Mounds defects that are critical to yield at the 10nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron SL650 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron SL650
- Inspection Type: Surface Roughness Analysis
- Target Defect: Mounds
- Process Step: Post-Oxidation
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 10nm
- Fab Location: Pyeongtaek Fab 2

This test case applies to all Teron SL650 systems deployed at Pyeongtaek Fab 2 for post-oxidation monitoring in the 10nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron SL650
Software Version: v14.6.519
Recipe: SURFACE_ROUGHNESS_ANALYSIS_10nm_POST_OXIDATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (170 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron SL650 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Surface Roughness Analysis' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Mounds defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 10nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 51 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 91% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.9% for Surface Roughness Analysis
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-28
Wafers Tested: 46
Total Defects Found: 3361
Defect Density: 1069.84 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 6.3%
Capture Rate: 86.9%
Test Duration: 93 minutes
System Uptime: 97.0%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron SL650 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Mounds at the 10nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
